transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Mark Jacobs (Hillside CTO), Sarah Lin (Head of ML), Raj Patel (Infra), Emily Cho (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Hillside is evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs hosted for production LLM serving. Primary drivers: isolation for PII, predictable latency for inference, cost controls, and ability to burst for nightly batch scoring. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick intros - I'm Alex, I run the AE motion for Redwood.
[00:12] Mark (Hillside CTO): Hey Alex. Mark here, Sarah and Raj and Emily from our side. We're evaluating options for running our customer-facing models.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya from SE. Happy to dive into perf and infra details today.
[00:28] Sarah (Hillside ML): Hi, quick note - our main requirement is sub-150ms p95 for single-turn scoring at 512 tokens for our fraud model, with ability to hit higher throughput for nightly batch runs.
[00:40] Raj (Infra): And we need strict data isolation, can't have tenant data leaving our VPC. We also have SAML SSO and centralized KMS.
[00:49] Alex: Totally. Broadly there are three modes - our Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For Hillside sounds like Dedicated or Private. Today can you walk us through current infra and traffic patterns?
[01:05] Mark: Sure. API traffic is mostly real-time scoring - steady 80 qps with spikes to 300 qps for peak windows. Nightly batch jobs run a few hours and peak at ~2k qps when we re-score backlog. Latency targets are strict for the real-time flow.
[01:23] Priya: Got it. When you say 80 qps steady, what's the average sequence length and model size?
[01:29] Sarah: Typical sequences around 350-600 tokens. We're running a fine-tuned 7B variant right now, planning to test a 13B in canary. Model is open-weight variant.
[01:38] Alex: OK so dedicated capacity is a good fit - you get reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and the ability to configure burst capacity. For your p95 target, we'd look at an allocation sized to hit the steady-state qps with headroom for p95 latency SLOs, plus a burst policy that spills into extra reserved or autoscaling capacity.
[01:57] Raj: How does the burst work - is it instant? We have concerns about noisy neighbors and also cost when burst triggers.
[02:06] Priya: Burst is configurable. You can set a baseline reserved pool and a burst bucket that is billed differently - think of it as reserved capacity + burst credits. Kernels and our routing layer will try to route to the reserved pool first; if that's saturated and latency SLOs are at risk, we route to dedicated burst instances or fallback to compatible model variants hosted in another pool. There is also KV cache and prefix caching to reduce load.
[02:32] Mark: Can that burst route to Hosted? That would be a data residency problem for us.
[02:36] Alex: For compliance-sensitive customers we can restrict burst to other dedicated capacity within your account/tenant or to Private deployment. We won't route to our public Hosted pool unless you opt in.
[02:49] Sarah: About isolation - what isolation guarantees do we get on Dedicated? Physical GPU tenancy or virtualized?
[02:56] Priya: Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated at the GPU and node level. You get reserved nodes that aren't shared with other customers. For even stricter requirements we offer Private VPC where compute sits inside your VPC or on-prem.
[03:12] Raj: Network wise, do you support private peering and static outbound IPs? Our security team wants to lock down egress.
[03:19] Alex: Yes, we support VPC peering, private links, and static egress IPs for outbound. We also integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management.
[03:26] Emily (Procurement): Timeline question - if we go Dedicated, what are typical procurement and lead times for reserving GPUs?
[03:33] Alex: Typical lead time for Reserved Dedicated capacity depends on region and hardware availability; for common configs we can provision within 2-4 weeks after contract; custom hardware or large clusters might be 6+ weeks. We can also start with a short-term pilot on our Hosted/Dedicated test cluster to speed up validation.
[03:49] Mark: Pricing - need ballpark: committed monthly vs burst unit pricing.
[03:54] Alex: I'll send a pricing sheet for 4x A100, 8x A100 and 16x configs with committed discounts and burst unit rates. Example: committed capacity is billed monthly at lower unit cost; bursts billed at on-demand higher rate. I'll provide exact numbers in the follow-up.
[04:12] Sarah: On the perf side, can you run a benchmark with our model and real input shapes? We want to measure p95 under realistic batching and KV-caching scenarios.
[04:20] Priya: Absolutely. We typically run a 48-hour benchmark window where we allow your team to run synthetic and real workloads against a dedicated test cluster. We'll instrument token-level latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates. We'll need sample prompts and a representative traffic replay.
[04:36] Raj: Are there any runtime differences for quantized models? We're looking at int8/4 quant options to reduce memory.
[04:44] Priya: Runtime supports quantized paths; latency can vary - quantization often reduces memory footprint and allows higher throughput at cost of slight accuracy delta. We'll recommend profiles per model. We also do kernel selection tuned to sequence length distribution.
[04:58] Mark: If we pin a model version for serving, can we do canary rollouts? We run frequent experiments and need safe rollbacks.
[05:06] Alex: Yes, rollouts (canary, A/B) are supported - you can route a percentage of traffic to a variant, observe metrics via Redwood Console, and automatically rollback on regression.
[05:16] Sarah: Need to make sure evals detect quality regressions - we have downstream accuracy metrics tied to the prompts.
[05:21] Priya: We can integrate your eval harness or run Redwood Optimize to monitor prompt-set regressions and alert on performance/quality drift.
[05:31] Speaker 1: (mumble) and what about audit logs?
[05:34] Alex: Audit logs, per-request tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns are available - logs can be shipped to your SIEM or stored in your account with retention policy.
[05:43] Raj: Any differences for multi-tenant models vs single-tenant heavy usage? We might have multiple product teams.
[05:50] Priya: You can create per-route and per-model isolation within your Dedicated cluster - namespaces, RBAC, and rate limits. Each team can have its own quotas.
[06:00] Mark: What about upgrades and maintenance windows? We need predictable maintenance not to disrupt peak windows.
[06:06] Alex: Maintenance windows are scheduled; for Dedicated we aim for minimal disruption and can coordinate upgrades during low-traffic windows. For strict SLAs, we offer maintenance deferrals for an additional support tier.
[06:17] Sarah: For the nightly batch, can we schedule pre-warmed nodes so warmup doesn't affect latency?
[06:22] Priya: Yes - pre-warmed workers and persistent KV cache help. For batch windows we recommend a separate batch pool that can be scaled up and down with autoscaling policies to avoid impacting real-time nodes.
[06:36] Emily: From procurement side, what contract terms around data retention and deletion do we need to watch?
[06:42] Alex: Standard terms include data deletion on termination, optional longer retention if you need audits, and options for customer-managed keys. We'll attach our DPA and security appendix.
[06:55] Mark: Are there any hard limits on GPU allocation per tenant? If we reserve a 16-GPU cluster, can we split it among teams?
[07:02] Priya: You can carve the cluster into pools and assign quotas - logical partitioning on top of physical nodes.
[07:09] Sarah: For the benchmark, we want to test both 7B and 13B variants, and measure cost per 1M tokens.
[07:16] Priya: We'll collect token counts, GPU hours, and provide a cost breakdown. Also measure latency distributions for both models.
[07:24] Raj: Network egress - do you support VPC endpoints and ability to restrict outbound domains?
[07:30] Alex: Yes, private endpoints, whitelist egress via proxy, and static egress IPs. We'll need your network team to share firewall rules.
[07:39] Mark: What's the plan for capacity scaling if we get a sudden growth? We want predictable headroom.
[07:46] Alex: You can commit to a baseline with predictable pricing and have burst credits for short spikes; plus reserved buffer and scheduled scale-up windows. For unpredictable hypergrowth we can negotiate step-up commits to increase capacity.
[08:00] Sarah: Any workstation for developer testing? We want dev/test access to smaller instances.
[08:06] Priya: We recommend separate dev clusters with smaller GPUs and lower-cost models for experimentation; they can be isolated from prod.
[08:14] Emily: Compliance question - do you support SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[08:18] Alex: Yes, we support SAML, OIDC, SCIM, and granular RBAC.
[08:23] Raj: A bit of nit - KV cache miss behavior and eviction policy? On long sequences we need predictable cache performance.
[08:30] Priya: We expose cache hit/miss metrics and you can tune TTLs and eviction. The cache is per-tenant and can be shared across nodes in the cluster. Eviction is LRU by default but configurable.
[08:42] Mark: Risk/concern - if a model update changes hallucination behaviour and we route to fallback, how do we detect quality regressions quickly?
[08:51] Priya: Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set evals on rollout and send alerts on quality regression; you can block rollouts if metrics drop.
[08:59] Alex: Ok let's capture next steps - we will send pricing and security docs and schedule the benchmark. Any other open questions?
[09:08] Sarah: Will you share an example SOW and support SLAs?
[09:12] Alex: Yes. We'll include SLA tiers and an example SOW.
[09:18] Mark: Procurement - next internal approval in two weeks, aiming for PO end of month.
[09:22] Emily: We'll confirm exact PO process, but that timeline sounds right.
[09:27] Priya: For the benchmark setup we'll need sample prompts, a traffic replay, and access to a containerized model bundle or HF/weights location.
[09:36] Raj: Ok I'll coordinate on the network and test data, but need to ensure PII is redacted for the test unless we use Private.
[09:45] Alex: Understood - we can run with anonymized data initially. If you need to use real PII, we'd propose Private or a VPC-hosted Dedicated cluster and an executed DPA.
[09:59] Mark: Great. Thanks everyone.
[10:02] Alex: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the pricing and docs.
[10:06] (call wraps)
